utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I shan't be taking this morning's witness because for the last week I have to make some appearances in front of another Chamber in another case, and somewhat surprisingly, that case is sitting this morning as well as this afternoon. So I shall have leave very shortly. Ms. Somers will being taking the witness. I notify the Court that as to this week's witnesses, we, and indeed the Defence, have suffered the inconvenience of the listed witness, Sir Martin Garrod, being cancelled at late notice, and not for the first time. We have, I think, managed to find a full week of evidence for you. His late cancellation was at the direction of the special representative of the Secretary-General in Kosovo, and I simply inform the Chamber that I'm going to write to him, explaining that of course although there are competing difficulties, when witnesses are listed to attend there are particular difficulties in late cancellation. On this occasion we were able to find substitute witness, and we have put that witness back now to, of course, much nearer the end of the trial. So I'm going to have to write in reasonably clear terms about the difficulties that we would face if we have another cancellation on short notice. I shan't do it in your name, but I will, as it were, rely on the requirements that you make to have your time filled whenever possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. While we're on that topic, I trust that apologies were sent to the witness from last week, who, through nobody's fault here but because of the Court's breakdown, we were unable to sit on Thursday and Friday in the court in which we had been booked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your apologies were sent. We quite understood all the problems. He was cooperative in the extreme, and I think he's now listed to return a week today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Beg your pardon. That was the original plan. He's now coming on Wednesday. But Ms. Somers will take this witness. I will, I hope, be in most of the week, but I shan't be in for all of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Nice. Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Examined by Ms. Somers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please state your full and correct name?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Stjepan Tuka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your date of birth is 25 December 1953?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Gojavici, in Fojnica municipality.

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, Fojnica, and I lived in Gojavici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are by ethnicity a Bosnian Croat?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You completed, in Sarajevo in 1972, technical school, with a specialisation in auto mechanics?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I believe it was '71.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are an auto mechanic by trade?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your military service in the JNA from 1973 to 1974, a total of some 15 months?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in reserve officer school for some five to six months in Karlovac?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive training in the Engineering Corps of the JNA as well as basic training and weaponry skills in battle situations?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the reserves as a Captain from 1982 until 1990, and were you in charge of a Territorial Defence unit in Gojavici?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of persons did you supervise in that unit? Were they armed persons?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: In case -- in case of an attack or something, then that unit would have been issued with weapons at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there nurses and elderly persons in these units and perhaps builders?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: They were part of the civilian defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you, in fact, in charge of that for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, if some combat operations took place, then I would be, yes, in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1990, were you relieved of your position as a reserve officer in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No. I was simply removed from the post of the command -- from the duty of the commander of that particular unit, but I did keep the rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that weapons for the Territorial Defence in Fojnica and Kresevo were kept at the JNA warehouse in Kiseljak barracks?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Quite. Those weapons were kept at the barracks at Kiseljak, but I do not know until when. Later on I heard from people who were with the Territorial Defence that those weapons were then taken away to the territory of the Ilijas municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is between Visoko and Sarajevo and that was under Serb control?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find yourself, at a later date, that this turned out to be true, that these weapons were in Serb hands?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, we could not get them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the ethnic composition of Fojnica municipality, percentage of Muslims, Croats and others?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: According to the census of 1990, I believe is when it was, there were 49 per cent of Muslims; 42 per cent of Croats; and 7 per cent were Yugoslavs and others, Serbs and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1991, when a war began in Croatia, on the territory of Croatia, initiated by the Serbs, did the Croats in Central Bosnia begin to organise and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, quite. We began to organise ourselves. I don't know. It was -- it was the former half of 1991. The reason was simple. We could see what was going on up there in Croatia, and we were expecting that the war would shortly be transferred to the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and we simply had to do something to protect people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this organising dangerous at the time because of the territory still being under JNA control? Under JNA control?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, of course it was dangerous, because the points and all the principal routes were controlled by JNA members, so yes, it was dangerous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the percentage of Serb officers in the JNA officer corps at the time?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, not exactly, but I heard that the figure was about 70 per cent of the Serbs and 30 per cent of others. But I don't know if the figure is accurate. That is from what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While the Croat community was organising, did the Muslim community also begin organising?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't know if they began to do that at that time, and whether they began. When the war began in April '93 [sic], the Muslims in Fojnica did have an organisation, but I really wouldn't be able to tell you when they began organising themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean the war which began in April of '92?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Beba Nasuf, and what was the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Beba Nasuf at that time was the commander of the Patriotic League. That was what the Muslims called their defence forces in the early days of the war, so those were organised Muslim formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that in municipalities where Croats were in the majority, many families removed their sons from the JNA, perhaps illegally?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1990, with the multiparty elections, which parties won the majority in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: The Party for Democratic Action and the Croat Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Party for Democratic Action was the Muslim party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you characterise the relations between the Muslims and the Croats as united and positive prior to any time of conflict in your area?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, they were normal. People lived normal life. They worked and cooperated with one another, and that was it. I don't think there was any particular tension.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the time the HDZ/BiH won, did you become involved?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall an Ante Beljo from Zagreb coming to your community and speaking to the Bosnian Croats about HDZ matters?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I do not remember him coming to our municipality, but I do remember listening to him somewhere, I mean that he was somewhere and that he delivered a speech, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this somewhere in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Nevenka Bosnjak-Mijatovic, whom I will refer to as Mrs. Bosnjak in future, was a member of the BiH parliament for Fojnica. Was she also involved in the HDZ in Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: She was, yes, of course. She was the HDZ president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did she ask you to do relating to the organisation of defence of Fojnica municipality?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: She asked me first if I would accept this task; that is, if I could help to organise the defence of the Croat people in the Fojnica municipality. I gave it a thought for a while, and then I agreed, and I said that -- yes, but that had to be the defence, and that only so was I ready to accept it, because otherwise I wasn't even professionally capable of organising some units which could launch some major attacks or something like that. I also said that if we are going to do that, I really do not care if people that I choose, that I select, are HDZ members or not. The only thing that will matter is whether they can do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the succession of the presidents of the HDZ/BiH, starting with Stjepan Kljuic, and if so, do you know what happened with Mr. Kljuic and who succeeded him?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Stjepan Kljuic was succeeded by Miljenko Brkic, I think, as far as I remember, but it was only for a very short while, and then I think that Mate Boban became the HDZ president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a difference in the political positions of Stjepan Kljuic and Mate Boban, and how would you characterise that difference?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: The difference -- well, truth to tell, there was a difference, yes. I heard Stjepan Kljuic was a man who was for Bosnia-Herzegovina, but Mate Boban, when making his speeches and at various meetings which I attended, he only mentioned the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Herceg-Bosna, and things like that. That is, reference was made that the time had come for the Croat soil, for the Croat turf, to join the mother country, Croatia; and I concluded on the basis of that that he was a little bit more extreme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You attended meetings that were HDZ/BiH meetings, and I would ask the usher to present Z8,1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Translations are available, I believe, in both French and English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tuka, if you look at the document, which is dated 30th of July, 1991, it is an agenda for a meeting of the HDZ/BiH at which you are listed as being present, as well as Dario Kordic. If you would turn, please, to Point -- it'll be after Tocka 3, essentially the last page in Serbo-Croatian. Would you indicate, please, what role Dario Kordic is to play with the Travnik regional community which is being formed? Does it indicate that he will be essentially coordinating these meetings?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps it does say here and I haven't read it yet, but I really don't remember what decisions those meetings took. It was a long time ago, and I really couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your name appears as being present. You accept that you were present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, if my name is here, then it means that I was there, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of your being involved with the HDZ, did you see Mate Boban at all? Did you ever personally see Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you able to estimate the number of times you may have seen him?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't know; could have been three or four, maybe five times. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dario Kordic with Mate Boban when Mate Boban normally addressed the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: He usually -- Mr. Kordic was usually present at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 20th of June, 1991, did you attend a meeting at the presidential palace in the office of President Tudjman in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that meeting a meeting of the HDZ/BiH, some of its members and leadership?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: As far as I could see, it was only a meeting of municipal representatives, and I could see from those who attended it there were representatives from Central Bosnia and the Bosnian Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to take from Ms. Ver Haag at this time the -- I'm sorry -- the photograph -- I beg your pardon -- which is labelled Z2784, and also to hand, for a moment, to the witness a copy. It should be at the back of the packet, of everyone's evidence packet. I should like to inform the Court that a blow-up of the colour original will be made for the Court. At this time we'll have to ask the Court to bear with us and look at the black and white which is at the back of the packet. I'm sorry, Your Honours. Is the photograph with you? Do you have it? Thank you. Good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tuka, the photograph which you have -- I'm sorry. The photograph which you have in front of you, both in colour and in black and white, is the black and white a copy of the colour photo?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If the usher could kindly show it to Mr. Tuka to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please describe the circumstances surrounding that photograph and who some of the central figures there are?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: This photo was made after the meeting in Zagreb where Ante Beljo, Gojko Susak spoke, as far as I know. After that, President Tudjman received his Banski Dvori and this was a souvenir photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking in the photo, the lady is who?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Oh. This is Dr. Nevenka Bosjnak, the president of the HDZ in Fojnica former.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the photo, looking to her right, looking as you look at it, who is next to her?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Why, Dr. Franjo Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the other side of Mrs. Bosjnak?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: It's -- I believe it's Ante Beljo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And next to Ante Beljo?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Ignjac Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And behind Ante Beljo, looking at him, on the left side, is that yourself?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No. This is Bruno Susnja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the other side?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then behind him also, as you said, is Bruno Susnja.

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the back, can you indicate if -- next to President Tudjman who is the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Oh. This is Martin Udovicic, I think, or Udovicic. I wouldn't know his surname correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And behind Mr. Udovicic is Dario Kordic, is that right, looking at the right?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the very edge, the gentleman with his arms folded is Ivica Santic?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How long were you in Zagreb for this meeting? How many days?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: It was one evening only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what was discussed?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: It was a long time ago, so I really cannot remember exactly what happened. I was in -- I was sort of lost or confused under the impression of the events and the place where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the only time in your life you have been to Banski Dvori and seen President Tudjman live?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall at that meeting, were there only representatives from Central Bosnia? Were there any representatives from Herzegovina at that particular meeting on the 20th of June?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, only Zdenko Cosic, who is originally from Herzegovina, was there, but I think he had a position in the HDZ for BH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then no other Herzegovinian representatives were there that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: With us on that occasion, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment. I want to speak to the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Steps are in hand to stop that building noise. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at the meetings of HDZ-BiH when criticisms were made? Do you recall criticisms having been made?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I remember that at one meeting there was some criticism, but where this was and when, I really am unable to determine.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If the usher would present -- or if the witness has Z2354. It should be in B/C/S and English. I apologise that there is not a French translation at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document are conclusions from a meeting of the Herzegovina regional community and the Travnik regional community on the 12th of November, and the witness is a signator to the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tuka, looking at this document, do you find on the very back page your signature, indicating that you were present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at point "C," which would be, I believe, on the second page, I want to draw your attention to one point, if you have any particular recollection of who raised the matter about: "Make even better military preparations for confrontation with all those forces which will attempt to stop this unavoidable process of the creation of a free Croatia state." Do you have any recollection or not?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I am unable to remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I have been asked to remind the registrar -- it's our error -- this has been previously tendered as Exhibit Z22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the Croats were to organise themselves in your community in the event of an attack, was there any type of plan to have the plan, in fact, or an understanding to have a joint defence between the Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No, there wasn't at the time until the war started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you form, at the request of Dr. Bosjnak, a headquarters for persons who would gather and who were experienced in military affairs?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Did you form, at your house, at the request of Dr. Bosjnak, a headquarters of persons who would be working in military affairs who would, in the event of an attack, be charged with the defence of Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time in Fojnica, do you recall that the Croat population was in any particular danger as it was surrounded by non-Serb municipalities and then somewhat to the west, Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: There was no realistic danger. Of course, it depended on developments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any perceived danger at the time from the Muslim community within Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've already seen a document of the Travnik regional community, which was formed in 1991, and you participated in meetings of the Travnik regional community?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which was founded by decision on 18 November of 1991, do you recall, as a member of the HDZ, a referendum being presented to your municipality as to whether or not HZ-HB should be founded?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Marinko Bosjnak?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: He was my closest associate during the preparations, and after the outbreak of the war he joined the command or -- I don't know how it's called -- the headquarters in Busovaca where Dario Kordic was and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first held military meetings in September of 1991, from Busovaca who was present, if you recall? Were there any figures such as Dario Kordic or perhaps Kostroman?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Pasko Ljubicic ever present?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Anto Sliskovic?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often were these meetings held and generally what types of matters did you deal with?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Usually once a week, sometimes once a fortnight, there were discussions about the results achieved in the organisation of defence. Then we discussed about the barracks in Kiseljak or Busovaca, and what should be done in the event that the Serbs attacked, and mainly such organisational matters were discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, issue various orders concerning the defence of communities in Bosnia against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue -- I will just show you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher, please, to point out Z324.1, Z375, Z375.1.

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. It's an order that when the war had begun. Yes, I did issue orders of this kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've jumped a little bit, but when the HVO was formed, what was your official position in Fojnica with regard to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I was the commander of the HVO armed forces in the municipality of Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Exhibit Z324.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise at this point; there is in English translation, but I will ask the witness to describe what it is.

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: This is a list of personnel assigned to positions at Paklarevo. This was the front line towards the Serbs, toward Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit Z375. Excuse me. The order is signed by yourself that you just mentioned, about Paklarevo. That is your signature on the order?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Not on this order. This was my assistant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it done under your command?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Z375. Could you explain what this is about, please, to the Court?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: This also is a document whereby a unit is being assigned to Paklarevo and indicating what this unit needs to be equipped with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you indicate needed to be provided? What type of equipment?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: For instance, the unit must have a communications officer, a medical officer complete with medical set, two snipers, two machine-guns per platoon, and then logistics support, first-aid dressing for every soldier, two combat sets for every soldier, one daily dry rations, one hand grenade, a helmet, a gas mask, each for one soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Z375.1. Would you explain this list, please, what it is, what it represents, and was it for the defence of territory?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: This is a list of soldiers carrying out orders and going only for the needs of defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, at Paklarevo?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in Fojnica, have a meeting with other municipality representatives, agreeing to join forces with the Muslims for the purpose of better defence?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. When the war started, that same day the politicians met and the president of the HDZ said -- or rather, she introduced me as the commander of the Croatian forces, and the president of the HDZ introduced Nasuf Beba as the commander of the BH army or, rather, the Patriotic League -- that is how it was called in those days -- and so it was that we immediately made certain arrangements, that tensions should not be heightened, that we should go among the population to calm people down because there was a great deal of panic. People simply didn't know what they should do and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the ZNG? What do those initials stand for, and did this have application of this type of meeting you just described, this type of alliance you described?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: A day after the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, and after this first meeting of ours, the municipal assembly of Fojnica met and adopted a decision to disband the Territorial Defence as a military organisation, as a military body for defence, and that the legal forces were the national guards corps. That is how we called them, and we imitated the name used in Croatia. It was decided that both would be legal military organisations, that we should take joint measures to ensure security of citizens and property. Similarly, the politicians, this whole municipal leadership, took a decision not to primped any solutions regarding the status of Bosnia-Herzegovina, regarding the kind of order that would be established, but rather that we should both accept the solutions agreed upon at a higher level, because we were conscious that that would be what would happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, I don't want to interrupt, but we've been going for some time. I'm conscious of the number of witnesses we have to hear this week, so if we can get through this preliminary part of the evidence more quickly --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- it would be a good idea. Mr. Tuka, if you could just concentrate on answering the questions, counsel will know what is relevant and what isn't. I don't want to, of course, cut you off, but it would be helpful if you would concentrate on just dealing with what you're asked. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In fact the witness pre-empted Question 32, so that helped us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the issue of weapons, can you describe quickly the first supplies of weapons that came in, and how did they come through to your territory?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Sometime in October, November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through what part of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: They came from the direction of Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally received weapons on two occasions. Can you describe these occasions and what you received?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. Once, in the Lasva Valley, I don't know the exact location, there were about 100 automatic rifles and 10 other "Argentines," as they were called. And then a second time I went to Grude and got about 200 automatic rifles for Kiseljak, Kresevo, and Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a total of 600 rifles, then? 200 per municipality?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any uniforms or any other materials through Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you explain briefly?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: A gentleman who was working in Germany, he raised some funds, or -- I don't know how; in any event, he got some uniforms of the German army. There was some more clothing and footwear, and on his way back, passing through Zagreb, he visited some acquaintances, and he loaded some anti-tank mines and some infantry weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this came to your territory?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The meetings -- I'm sorry; the troops who were stationed at the Hotel Jezero, could you explain briefly what that stationing was about and how long that lasted?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: We had formed a joint unit of Muslims and us, 25 each, 50 in all, and they should be together. When the war broke out, we set up checkpoints, primarily to avoid any thefts and to ensure security of the whole municipality. This unit was there for about a month or two. Later on, it proved to be unnecessary in view of the way the situation developed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, did the joint patrols continue until April of 1993, as well as joint checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive an order, do you recall receiving an order in the beginning of June of 1992 which indicated that the Croatian military units of Bosnia and Herzegovina would henceforth be called the Croatian Defence Council, with its central military headquarters in Mostar, perhaps originally elsewhere, in Grude? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a military headquarters in Busovaca as well?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: For the region of Central Bosnia, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the role of Dario Kordic and Ignjac Kostroman in Central Bosnia as you understood it at that time?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: At the time, they were coordinators of all these events in Central Bosnia. They organised meetings. As far as I know, that is what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were commander of the HVO in Fojnica from April of '92 until May of '93. Did you ever get any formal instructions on how to structure units once you became the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you told?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I received an order at the end of 1992 that brigades needed to be formed, and together with the municipalities of Kiseljak, Kresevo, and Fojnica, we were supposed to form one brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a rank structure at this time?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No. Not in our case, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a military police unit formed, and by whom was it commanded initially?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I know what was happening in our area. We formed a military police unit, and the commander was Dragan Simunic at first, and later on, Mirovucic -- no, Nikica Miletic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What role did Dr. Bosjnak play officially? Was she an officer?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, she was responsible for the organisation of the medical care -- I mean, the military medical service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the principal purpose, as you understood it, of the HVO at the time of its initiation, protection from Serb aggression, and if so, did that change?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: At that time, that was certainly so. But then some incidents happened, if I remember well, at Prozor, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and the situation began to change in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of an incident around May 1992 involving Dario Kordic and the local JNA commander?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't lead about this, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you discuss, please, what you know about the Serb army leaving the territory in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, by and large, by agreement, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between whom?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Between local commanders in those barracks and those local commanders and politicians, I mean in municipalities. I know about Kiseljak, and I believe the same thing happened in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any role played by Dario Kordic in dealing with these local JNA commanders?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't, but I guess that he was the one who conducted negotiations in Busovaca, but not in Kiseljak, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of Busovaca having been bombed, and if so, do you know why?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I know it was shelled. Why, exactly, I don't know, but I heard from some people that the agreement that had been reached about the departure from the barracks had not been complied with fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear who reached the agreement?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, those representatives of the authorities and barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, excuse me: I did not react straight away, but the witness is saying that he doesn't really know that, that he only heard that, and I do not think there is any need to examine him further on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He was asked if he had heard who reached the agreement; he said the representatives of the authority and the barracks. Now, do you want to pursue that, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to just focus, if I may, and if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can do so, but in a non-leading fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not Mr. Kordic was among those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, that's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Quite plainly -- no, be quiet for a moment. Do you know who the authorities were who reached these agreements?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Dario Kordic, Ignjac Kostroman, and one of the -- I don't really remember what was the name of the representative of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the Serbs abandoned or left the Kiseljak barracks, are you aware of what happened to those barracks? To whom were they given?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive instructions from Mostar about setting up computerised radio communications, and if so, could you describe the system?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, we were given instructions, and a man who was knowledgeable about those things came, and all we had to do was provide a computer and a radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the system called Paket communications?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, that's the system, the computerised one, which is one system, an integrated system, and it was integrated for the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find it to be a reliable system?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of details were evidenced or written or transmitted on any communication on the Paket radio system?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, everything that was necessary. One could use -- or rather transmit by the system messages, orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And typically would they include a sender, an author, a recipient, a date, time, as well as the content of the message?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were signatures, actual signatures, transmittable?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you accept as authoritative an order that came over the Paket communications system with a name -- let's say, for example, Tihomir Blaskic -- even though there was no signature?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe when you first met Tihomir Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Sometime in May, if I remember well, of '91 -- '92; excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any observations about -- excuse me; did you ever observe Tihomir Blaskic and Dario Kordic in public together?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: When Tihomir Blaskic became the commander for Central Bosnia, then yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally attend meetings and functions where you saw them together, personally?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to take an oath of allegiance to the HVO armed forces in Fojnica sometime in July or August of '92, and if so, could you describe the scenario?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: We were ordered to line up the units so that they could take the solemn oath of allegiance. So we all met at the stadium, the football playing grounds in Fojnica, and organised a small celebration and swore the allegiance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many men took the oath?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I believe it was between 800 and 1.000. I wouldn't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if the wording of the oath specified which country you were defending?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you do not remember, or no, it did not specify the country?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Not -- mentioned only that we would defend our homeland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the guests of honour at that particular ceremony?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic, Blaskic, Kostroman, representatives of the Muslims, of the church, politicians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if Mr. Kordic and Kostroman were in uniform?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, they were in uniform?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have dealings with a Captain Sartre from UNPROFOR, and under what circumstances? Why did you have to meet with him?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. That gentleman visited me at the time when an UNPROFOR plane was downed, the one which was taking aid to Sarajevo, and it fell in the territory of my municipality. That gentleman came to my command and we talked, and then he asked me if I could establish contact between him and my superiors. We went together to Busovaca, and I said that this is where the Central Bosnian command was and he stayed there. I believe he stayed behind talking to Kostroman, Kordic, and others who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember where you took him in Busovaca to see Kordic and Kostroman?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I think it was Tisovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it guarded?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, there were guards, naturally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if Dario Kordic, at that time, was a Colonel in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not recall, or he was not?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: He was not. As far as I know, there were no ranks. Nobody had any rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware if he ever took on a rank, and if so, do you know for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I know that he did have a rank, but what was the purpose of that, I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe, please, the -- oh, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequently did you go to Busovaca, if you used to go to Busovaca, and what did you do there when you went?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, like that. We would go sometimes for -- every week or a fortnight for consultation to see, just to keep in touch, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom did you see there?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Dario Kordic usually, and Ignjac Kostroman, then Marinko Bosjnak arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he use the occasion to discuss matters pertaining to fund-raising, transport, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: At times; at times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you comment on the type of uniform an HVO officer would typically wear? Specifically, was there any indication of rank or was there a patch?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Whilst I was what I was, the uniforms were almost identical, I mean, both the soldiers and commanders. They would have an HVO flash on the left sleeve and that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you comment on the use of colour ribbons or kerchiefs -- probably "ribbons" would be the best term -- and what they were used for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Ms. Somers. We've been almost one hour in session, and the president had asked you to focus on facts, because there are certain things which by now the Tribunal is quite aware of and quite familiar with. We're not at the beginning of the process. So the uniforms, the ranks, and things like that, we are informed about that; we are quite familiar with it. So will you please do not keep this witness telling us things that we already know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The emphasis of my question at this point was on the use of ribbons, and I'm not clear that the Court has had testimony on the use of ribbons. There is a specific point to this. It ties up with other witnesses. If I may just have the witness answer this particular question, if he can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Excuse me, if I may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. I'll repeat quickly. Are you familiar with the use of colour ribbons, perhaps on the shoulders of HVO uniforms, and what purpose would those serve?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Those ribbons were worn in combat operations. They were carried by members of all the armies for the purposes of identification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Fojnica substantially supportive of the positions coming from the more nationalist groups within the HDZ? Was it willing, for example, to put up Croatian flags and have Croatian indicia throughout its institutions?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Oh. Well, it wasn't. We tried to solve it to the mutual satisfaction, and we'd agreed not to put up either Croat or Muslim flags until the end of the war, until we would see how the situation would be solved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever informed by Dario Kordic that this attitude was unsatisfactory?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, yes. Yes. There was mention of that. There was mention of that. But we tried to explain that we're trying to gain time, that it wouldn't be a solution, and if we tried that, then it would produce major tension and probably even an armed conflict, and that was what we wanted to avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should ask for the witness not to be led by these questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when the Busovaca-Kiseljak main route, main road, was blocked by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: It was between January or February 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Were there any deaths of HVO soldiers as a result of this particular blocking?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I think there was a skirmish, and I believe two HVO members were killed in it, somewhere around Kacuni. There were also a few wounded, and they were taken to the hospital in Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when your units under your command in Fojnica were ordered to become part of the Josip Ban Jelacic Brigade in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: After Ban Jelacic Brigade was formed. That's when our brigade was formed. Then our unit was part of that brigade, but then it was reorganised and our unit was made to join the Busovaca Brigade, the brigade which was in Busovaca. Then sometime in April 1993 we were then ordered to place ourselves under the command of the brigade in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who headed the Josip Ban Jelacic Brigade in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: The first commander was Ivica Rajic, and then he was removed and Mijo Bozic came. But when the war broke out, Mijo, I think, was also removed, and I think it was Mario Bradara who was appointed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To clarify something, was there a time when you both reported to Kiseljak and were yet subordinate to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear comments made by a Nikola Perica about the way the HVO in Fojnica was operating compared to other units of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, there were all sorts of comments. One of them was how could it be that only two men were killed in Fojnica and there were as many as 20 killed in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Perica coming from inside Bosnia or was he an outsider?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: He had been born in Bosnia, yes, but he was working in America, as far as I know. And in the beginning of the war he came to Croatia, and as the war spread out so he came to us too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him after the conflict broke out between the Muslims and the Croats? Did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to meet with Colonel Blaskic, whether informally or formally, after the brigade was restructured in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever pay a visit to Bozo Rajic, the vice-president of Herceg-Bosna, or one of the vice-presidents, in February of 1993, and if so, where and with whom?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. We went to visit him in Mostar. Dr. Bosnjak was with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the visit? What did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: We thought that perhaps we would hear from him more about the real political objectives, because it was quite evident that one thing was being said and a completely different thing was being done on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Bosnjak know Rajic? Was there a particular reason you chose this official?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, yes. They were friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if any questions were asked by Bozo Rajic about the course of action being taken in Fojnica, and how did you answer those questions?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Oh, it was not -- as far as I can remember, it -- Fojnica was the only place which was addressed. We were discussing politics, the positions of Mate Boban, by and large that we were being told to introduce the HVO power, and she said it was easy to do in Western Herzegovina, in localities which had always been held by Croats, but it was difficult to do that in Central Bosnia with such a mixed population and where any attempt of that kind would simply exacerbate tensions and eventually lead to a conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not there was a discussion about instigating fights or conflicts between the Muslims and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No, I don't. No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to see anyone else, any other high official, after visiting Bozo Rajic?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Milivoj Petkovic, the HVO commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what you discussed with Mr. Petkovic and where you met him?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: It was in his office. We did not talk long; it could have been 10 or 15 minutes. And in a nutshell, he told me that he had already received a delegation from Fojnica, that he was aware of what was going on over there, that I should cooperate with Blaskic more, and that was about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any discussion about your relationship with the Muslim community in Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: At some point he told me, verbatim, "What's that secret alliance, collusion with Muslims up there?" Then I said it was no collusion, that it was a decision of the municipal assembly and we were simply trying to put it through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In March of 1993, were you informed again about a change in the relationship to the Kiseljak brigade and where your units would fall in terms of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. I already said so, that our unit was to be attached, to join the brigade in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I will present, just to get into evidence, Z744A. 744A. Well, 744 would be in Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just confirming what you have just said, does this order, dated 20 April, confirm the replacement of the Fojnica 3rd Battalion to be subordinated to the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade and under the command of the Kiseljak Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No, it is not this document, the one that I have here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you should have one dated 4/20/93, signed -- not signed; it's a Paket communication from Tihomir Blaskic, Z744.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Does the usher have it? If not ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that confirming the restructuring you just discussed?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, when you come to a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Certainly. I think now would be good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, we'll adjourn. Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask the Court's indulgence for a moment. I was able to locate two documents that I did not have at my fingertips, and just to return to one point which had been previously covered, Z384 and Z386, very quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tuka, looking at document Z384 briefly, this is an order or a request made to you and Mrs. Bosnjak in Fojnica from Dario Kordic. What is being requested? What is the subject matter of this request?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't know, but what I see from this text, it is the replacement of Mr. Dragan Tolo, who was commander of the civilian police. So I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only issue is that you are in the request; thank you. And briefly, Z386: Does this confirm that appointment? The appointment, that is, of Nikola Perica?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't know. I never saw this, nor was Mr. Perica appointed to that post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continuing to the later part of our examination, do you recall, on or about the 16th, 17th of April, 1993, visiting Kiseljak barracks and having a discussion with Boro, Bozic, Bradara, and Lucic?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Boro? I don't know whether his name is Jozic -- Jozo Boro; yes, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the discussion about? What were your concerns?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: They told me that they were discussing an order they had received about the situation in Central Bosnia, and that they should join in combat operations, and that they are reviewing what should be done and how.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any particular worry expressed about carrying out this order? Do you know what the order was about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I saw that they were quite worried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Probably because of the seriousness of the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, around that time, receive a message from Kiseljak Brigade headquarters, early morning, concerning the starting of an action by the Kiseljak Brigade?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later learn which villages were to have been involved or attacked in that action?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't know if the villages were attacked in that action, but later, we learnt that it was Rotilj, Visnjica, Gomionica, and some others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Gromiljak also included?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Probably, because it is in the same region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you order Sladjo Jukic to do anything at that time in response?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes, to protect this border area with our municipality. I told Sladjo to try, with the commander of the BH army, with whom he cooperated, as he was commander of the HVO in the area, that they should try to do something together, organise some kind of patrols, so that the people would feel safer and that no incidents could be staged by people out of control or any kind of conflict should break out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your units take part in any of the actions in the Lasva Valley on villages around the 16th of April, 1993, and particularly, did you have any relationship to the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any orders about state of battle readiness for your units?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Oh, yes. There were a lot of orders around that time. Combat readiness needed to be raised to the highest level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive an order from Tihomir Blaskic concerning an attack that you were to initiate on the village of Dusina in Fojnica municipality?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask if the usher could please present Z709, and also Z733, which I will address quickly first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at 733, this order from Tihomir Blaskic about taking Gomionica, was that order ever sent to your unit?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Z709, can you please look at point 2 and indicate what the assignment was that you were given, the order was that you were given by Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: The order said that I should carry out a combat operation on the village of Dusina or make a breakthrough towards Busovacke Staje and link up with the forces defending Sebesic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date of that order is 18 April 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do in response to this order?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I informed my associates, because it was said here that we could choose one or other alternative, and as we had already established cooperation, we decided to leave aside this order and not to carry it out, because the consequences would really have been unforeseeable at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you view the consequences as dangerous and were there issues that you chose to inform Colonel Blaskic about?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: It was dangerous if an attack were to be launched anywhere. The war would have automatically spread and enveloped the whole area. But we had hoped that some kind of an agreement, an arrangement would have been made. It's easier before a war begins. Afterwards, it would be difficult to halt it. So simply we were not ready for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the ethnic composition of the village of Dusina, Muslim to Croat?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Two-thirds Muslim, one-third Croat. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, at the time the order came down, of any difficulties, tensions, or conflicts between the two groups in Dusina?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: There was always some tension because the local commander in Dusina was a man who did not obey orders from his commander in Fojnica but, rather, collaborated with some people in Konjic. He was rather an extremist, and he was on the very edge of our municipality. So we sort of let him be, and be master in his little village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I repeat: At the time of this order. Was there any perceptible threat to the Croat population that you felt the need to react to?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: At that moment, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, respond in writing to Colonel Blaskic about your views on executing or not that order?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. I did that after his warning that I had to carry out orders or I would be replaced.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher and the registrar, please, to take what has already been tendered as Z731 -- it is duplicated in a different number on our list -- but Z731 and also to present Z748 to the witness. Actually, 48 and 49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the number, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, what is the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The number of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It should -- the former Exhibit 731, Z731. I do not know if it was duplicated in this packet. It was not, I'm told. If there is not one handy, my copy is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you can deal with it without putting the document up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. It should be ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for the poor quality of the copy, but, Mr. Tuka, can you identify what this order is, who it is from, and what the consequences were? Can you see it okay in Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom is this order?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: From Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dated what date?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: 19th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the essence of the document? What does he tell you?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Because of the situation, I have to carry out orders issued; otherwise, I would be replaced and held accountable in accordance with the regulations of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Exhibit Z748, this is a letter which you drafted to Colonel Blaskic. What did you explain to the Colonel? This letter dated 20 April 1993.

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't know. It was simply a spontaneous reaction whereby I was a bit angry, and I said that I was aware of my duty when accepting to organise the Croatian people in Fojnica but that I was not ready, before my own conscience and before other people, to answer for what would happen if I had carried out certain orders which directly lead to killings and generally to war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Killings of civilians?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: This applies to everyone. Of course, once the war begins, the civilians die as well, because it was very difficult to separate soldiers from civilians. They were all mixed together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you form any opinions about the strategic reason, on the part of the HVO command, for attacking Dusina with regard to the BiH forces?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No. I think that at that point in time the important thing was to start the conflict anywhere, simply for the conflict to escalate throughout.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If the usher would present Z749.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the order which you received from Colonel Blaskic in response to your letter indicating that you would not carry out the order?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is the response to that letter, but in any event, it is an order whereby I was relieved of my duty and Mr. Drago Simunic was appointed to replace me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This order signed by Blaskic, dated 20th April 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. It reached me by Paket. There was no signature, but there was the name of Mr. Blaskic written there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Z745, 746, and 747, in that order. On 745, what is the statement? What is the essence of the statement and by whom is it sent and to whom is it sent?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I think that this statement -- no, I'm sure it was sent by representatives of the Muslim people to representatives of the Croatian people and the authorities at the time; that is, to the president of the Croatian Democratic Community, to us in the headquarters, and to Naza Turka [phoen], the commander of the HVO or, rather, the president of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they ask that you not be removed, that your removal not be considered because of your peace efforts?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Something along those lines, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Z746, which is a press release on a joint meeting of the Muslim and Croat representatives of Fojnica. I apologise for the poor copy in Serbo-Croatian. This is a reaction by which bodies to the order to have you replaced?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: The Municipal Assembly of Fojnica, the commanders or, rather, representatives of military units of both peoples, the Franciscan Monastery of Fojnica, the Fojnica Islamic community, Napredak, Preporod, as is written there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Z747. This is a decision by a number of bodies as well to the command of the Ban Jelacic Brigade, dated 20 April 1993. Is this also a rejection of the decision or order to have you removed. And who authored this?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. It is also another decision written by the -- signed by the command of the 3rd Battalion, the Fojnica HVO, the Croatian Democratic Community, the Franciscan Monastery, the Croatian Cultural Society.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Z764, please. Is this a document, dated 20 April 1993, signed by yourself to the command?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain, please, what you are telling the command?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the message here?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: I told the command by this report that I accept the replacement and that on that day -- that is, on the 20th of April at 4.00 p.m. -- the meeting of the command would be held, at which the handing over of the duty will take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, was your position ever handed over to another person, specifically Simunic?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Mr. Simunic didn't want to accept. And then later on orders were received naming Simo Simic [phoen], Marinko Puco [phoen], Vlado Kapentanovic, but all of them refused to accept the position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain in that position essentially de facto for a period of time, let's say up until May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. I remained for another 10 or 15 days because there was no one to replace me. Nobody wanted to. All of these people insisted that I stay on, that I should continue for a time. However, sometime around the 10th of May I could no longer perform that duty because it had really become intolerable, and I simply left the command. Actually, I convened all the commanders and told them, explained to them once again the situation as it was, that I was no longer a legitimate commander and that in continuing I was committing a criminal act and that I had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If the usher could present Z892.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the witness when he decided to leave the post of the commander and the support he received. He explained it by saying the situation had become unbearable, and that if he continued he would be committing a criminal offence. Could the witness please explain why is that so and why the situation has become unbearable and why would he be committing an act which would be interpreted as a criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Well, it's quite simple. Simply because the orders were not being sent to my name. As a matter of fact, my superiors had relieved me of office, and whatever I did or might do in case of a danger of war or anything, I would be doing it on my own initiative. Secondly, there was also a group, rather strong, which brought pressure to bear on me every day. One day even fire was opened on my house when I was sleeping there with my wife and my children. I simply had to leave, because otherwise I would have been killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the orders were not being sent to you, but they were being sent in the name of whom? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. They were sent to the commander of that unit, commander of the 3rd Battalion, Nikola Subic-Zrinjski. That was that. Without the name.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was the commander, without specifying the name; is that so?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tuka, pursuant to the questions asked by Judge Bennouna, if you could take a look at Z892, a rather unwieldy sized document. Does this document confirm -- the document sent on the 7th of May, 1993, does it confirm that orders were sent to commander of the Busovaca Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade as well as the Fojnica commander battalion, with no name? And is there, at the end of the document, an indication that your activities or actions constituted grounds for disciplinary action and possible criminal charges with a competent military prosecutor, threat of which will be done?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. I would merely add, up here, when receiving the order, more often than not the name of the commander was never put there. Sometimes, yes, it figured in it; but as I really felt removed from office -- that is, I realised I had lost the authority and was not enjoying the support of my superior command in Vitez, and I did not enjoy the support of my superior command in Kiseljak, and I also had trouble with groups in my place, so that this was the only solution for me. And this also shows that I was guilty of some misdemeanour, of some disciplinary transgressions, and that I was supposed to be called to account.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tuka, during the time that you were commander in Fojnica, was there ever an open, violent conflict between the Muslim and Croat communities?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: No. Yes, detention went up, but there was no conflict; there was no armed incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to try to contact Muslim representatives, at the request of some of the elderly Croat citizens, in order to try to negotiate some type of peaceful resolution at the monastery?

utterances.speaker: Stjepan Tuka
utterances.text: Yes. When the war had started, and after some time, there were already casualties and fatalities, and a group of those elderly people called me and said, "Well, look, come, do you think you could do something about it?" Because they thought I still enjoyed some authority, some command in some respect on the Muslim side, and perhaps I could do something about it. So I did try something, but failed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
